gaps.what: A separate state: the row duplicates the Sultanate of Bengal (956 of 957 cells inside its 1529 shape) and runs a year and a half past the dynasty's end; merge into sultanate-of-bengal.
Sur land east of Agra after Panipat 1556, the Muhammad Shahi rulers and the seat of the Orissa Afghans, Multan and upper Sindh dates, Raisen, Kalinjar's fate, and any area figure.
Ruler strip, dates of the early conquests (Satyamangalam to Coimbatore), the 1772, 1784 and 1787 treaty terms, and when Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur, Dindigul and the Baramahal were taken.
Independence from Vijayanagara, the reign list 1601-1609, Ramnad, Pudukkottai and palayam boundaries, an area figure.
Vallamprakara date, Vijaya Raghava's reign events, Bijapur and Mysore pressure, Alagiri, boundaries.
Unification-table rows for 1761 (Chaule and Kahule), 1765 (Balaju, Lutikot) and 1768 (Bara, Parsa, Hilwal, Bettia); ruler strip.

problems: hussain-shahi-dynasty is the same state as sultanate-of-bengal (the page: the dynasty ruled the Sultanate of Bengal 1494-1538; its Cliopatria shape lies 956/957 cells inside Cliopatria's Bengal 1529 shape; the sa-04-c dossier already runs to 6 April 1538 with its own 1534 keyframe). The one keyframe is marked wrong with a correction pointing at the Bengal outline; merge or alias it, or Bengal is drawn twice in 1534-1538. Cliopatria also runs the row to 1539, a year and a half past the dynasty's end (sur-empire_1538 covers 1538-1539).

sur-empire is one state 1538-1593 with rename events in 1557 and 1564 (Muhammad Shahi, Karrani); the Sur Empire page ends in 1556. A rule-2 split at 1556/1557 is possible and would make a Muhammad Shahi / Karrani sultanate of Bengal (1553-1576, Orissa to 1593) whose shapes are now in this dossier.

kingdom-of-mysore runs 1399 to 9 August 1947, against Cliopatria's 1572-1799, because no other dossier covers the princely state; cut at 1799 if the orchestrator prefers (drop the 1800 keyframe and the 1831-1947 events). The Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan period stays inside one state (rename events 1761, 1782, 1799).
mughal-empire dates the Orissa gain 1595 at confidence 1; sur-empire has the conquest of Orissa ending in 1593 (Cliopatria ends the Sur row in 1594). One of the two should move.

thanjavur-maratha-kingdom founds in early 1676 after Venkoji beats Alagiri; nayaks-of-thanjavur ends 1675 (Venkoji captures Thanjavur, per the Thanjavur Nayak page) with Madurai's 1673-1675 hold written as an occupation in both Nayak dossiers. Cliopatria runs the Nayak row to 1676.

Page budgets exceeded: sur-empire 6 of 5, kingdom-of-mysore 6 of 5, nayaks-of-madurai 7 of 5 (pages opened for the Mysore dossier were reused for the Coimbatore loss and the 1655 war). hussain-shahi-dynasty used 2, nayaks-of-thanjavur 2, gorkha-kingdom 3.

gorkha-kingdom was written in an earlier run of this batch and kept unchanged under the resume rule; it validates (0 errors, 0 warnings). All ten Cliopatria shapes are marked wrong (modern Nepal drawn back to 1588); the 1769-1787 shapes duplicate the nepal dossier of sa-05-f.
WebFetch of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tirumala_Nayak returned url_not_found; the article loaded as Thirumalai_Nayak and is the cited page. No page failed in the end.

british-empire and republic-of-india are counterparts of kingdom-of-mysore (1769, 1792, 1799; 1947); neither dossier was present when the validator ran, which raises no warning but leaves the pairing unchecked.

No area figure was available on any page for sur-empire, nayaks-of-madurai, nayaks-of-thanjavur, hussain-shahi-dynasty or gorkha-kingdom, so the infobox-versus-Cliopatria area comparison was made only for kingdom-of-mysore (205,000 km2 for 1779 against 91,000 km2 in Cliopatria).
